{{nihongo|'''Kunigami Shrine'''|國神神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echizen Province]].

'''Kunigami Shrine''' (くにがみじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Maruoka Town, {{ill|Sakai, Fukui|ar|ساكاي (فوكوي)|azb|ساکای، فوکوئی|bg|Сакаи (Фукуи)|ce|Сакаи (Фукуи)|ceb|Sakai-shi (distrito sa Hapon)|de|Sakai (Fukui)|es|Sakai (Fukui)|eu|Sakai (Fukui)|fa|ساکای، فوکوئی|fi|Sakai (Fukui)|fr|Sakai (Fukui)|gl|Sakai, Fukui|hy|Սակաի (Ֆուկուի)|id|Sakai, Fukui|it|Sakai (Fukui)|ja|坂井市|ko|사카이시 (후쿠이현)|mzn|ساکای، فوکوئی|nl|Sakai (Fukui)|pl|Sakai (Fukui)|ro|Sakai, Fukui|ru|Сакаи (Фукуи)|simple|Sakai, Fukui|sv|Sakai, Fukui|tl|Sakai, Fukui|tr|Sakai, Fukui|tt|Сакаи (Фукуи)|uk|Сакай (Фукуй)|ur|ساکائی، فوکوئی|uz|Sakai (Fukui)|vi|Sakai, Fukui|war|Sakai, Fukui|zh|坂井市|zh_classical|坂井市|zh_min_nan|Sakai-chhī (Hukui)|zh_yue|坂井|qid=Q990342}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|Q133879|qid=Q133879}}. Its former shrine rank was prefectural shrine. It enshrines Prince Maruko, a son of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|Q349277|qid=Q349277}}.

===History===
Listed as “Kunigami Shrine” of {{ill|Sakai District, Fukui|Q7402764|qid=Q7402764}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}, it is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} founded before 1200<ref name="board">Information board within the shrine grounds</ref>. According to the shrine tradition recorded in the *Shrine Register*, the shrine originated when the placenta of Prince Maruko, the second son of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|Q349277|qid=Q349277}} and Yahime, was buried at the place where the prince was born, called “Maruoko” (磨留古乎加), and a Shinmei shrine was established there<ref name="board" /><ref name="jinjacho">[http://www.jinja-fukui.jp/detail/index.php?ID=20151027_104515 Fukui Prefecture Shrine Association]</ref>.

Thereafter, it received protection and donations from successive lords of Maruoka Castle<ref name="board" /><ref name="jinjacho" />.

nî|zh_yue|1908年|zu|1908|qid=Q2056}}, it was specified as a shrine to receive offerings of sacred coins and ritual sticks<ref name="jinjacho" />.

The {{ill|1948|Q5165|qid=Q5165}} (Shōwa 23) {{ill|1948 Fukui earthquake|Q4389555|qid=Q4389555|lt=Great Fukui Earthquake}} on June 28 caused the shrine buildings and trees to collapse and burn, but on July 15, {{ill|1962|Q2764|qid=Q2764}}, the main hall (Shinmei-zukuri), offering hall, and worship hall were rebuilt. In {{ill|1982|Q2436|qid=Q2436}}, as a commemorative project marking the 20th anniversary of reconstruction, a treasure hall was newly built and a sacred fence erected<ref name="jinjacho" />.

===Cultural Properties===
Among its many cultural assets are the “Hanging Scroll of the Hakusan Pilgrimage Mandala, color on silk,” dating back to the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}} (designated a cultural property of Fukui Prefecture<ref>{{Cite web|ja|author= |year= |url=http://info.pref.fukui.jp/bunka/bunkazai/sitei/kaiga/itiran.html |title=Fukui Prefecture Designated Tangible Cultural Properties (Hanging Scroll of the Hakusan Pilgrimage Mandala, color on silk) |publisher=Fukui Prefecture |accessdate=2018-02-16}}</ref>), as well as the “Heavenly Treasure Sword,” said to have been dedicated by {{ill|Honda Shigeaki|Q10517896|qid=Q10517896}}, lord of Maruoka Castle, and the Senju Kannon of Jambudvīpa gold. Within the shrine grounds is also a stone lantern dedicated by {{ill|Arima Michizumi|Q10517531|qid=Q10517531}}, the final lord of the {{ill|Maruoka Domain|Q10863481|qid=Q10863481}} who also served as a shogunate {{ill|Rōjū|Q1196812|qid=Q1196812}}<ref name="board" />.

===Treasures===
* '''Hanging Scroll of Hakusan Toyohara Mandala, color on silk'''
: Said to have been produced in the Muromachi period, it is regarded as an important historical artifact of {{ill|Hakusan Faith|Q11579557|qid=Q11579557}}<ref name="岩崎27-28p">{{Cite book|ja|author=Iwasaki Shinnosuke |title=Folk Tales and Legends of Echizen Maruoka |publisher=Iwasaki Shinnosuke |year=1979 |page=27–28 |isbn=}}</ref>.
* '''Heavenly Treasure Sword'''
: A treasured sword dedicated by Honda Shigeaki, lord of Maruoka. The scabbard features {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=inlay work}}, and the {{ill|tsuba|Q1758043|qid=Q1758043}} (handguard) is made of gold. The scabbard is said to be decorated with *kan-shippō*. As of 2019 (Reiwa 1), it is preserved as a treasure of Kunigami Shrine<ref name="岩崎27-28p"/>.
* '''Senju Kannon of Jambudvīpa Gold'''
: In {{ill|862|Q24993|qid=Q24993}} (Jōgan 4), it was brought back from {{ill|Tang dynasty|Q9683|qid=Q9683}} by the monk Shinnyo of Settsu and is housed in a {{ill|Zushi|Q19993032|qid=Q19993032}} made of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=ebony}}. Seven ring-like ornaments hang from the halo of the Kannon, with their bases made of gold, silver, and {{ill|shakudō|Q11635994|qid=Q11635994}}, inlaid with red, blue, and white jewels. The zushi is carved with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=lotus flowers}}, and its curtain is adorned with beautiful gold and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=lapis lazuli}}<ref name="岩崎27-28p"/>.
